if: the transaction is a form of supply of goods or services or both — sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal
it is made or agreed to be made for a consideration
it is made by a person in the course or furtherance of business
then: the transaction IS a supply for the purposes of the CGST Act, and s.12 or s.13 must then fix its time of supply
note: All three limbs are conjunctive on the face of the clause. 'agreed to be made' is included, so an executory agreement can already be a supply. This clause does NOT decide goods-versus-services — s.7(1A) sends that to Schedule II, which is not extracted here.

evidence.quote: all forms of supply of goods or services or both such as sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal made or agreed to be made for a consideration by a person in the course or furtherance of business
